A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EfficientViM and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and supplementary material. Relocated experiments and renumbered displays can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original ImageNet classification, COCO detection and instance segmentation, architectural ablations, and runtime and memory measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds ADE20K semantic-segmentation results in Table 7.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the HSM-SSD operations, single-head design, multi-stage fusion, and model specifications in Table 2 remain unchanged. The new SemanticFPN experiment uses the existing EfficientViM backbone.

E1.justification: V2 adds ADE20K semantic segmentation, materially extending task coverage beyond ImageNet classification and COCO detection and instance segmentation. The existing COCO and high-resolution ImageNet evaluations are retained despite moving between the main text and supplement.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in matched existing experiments is unchanged. The new ADE20K comparison uses PVTv2-B0, FastViT-SA12, and EdgeViT-XXS, backbones already evaluated in v1's COCO comparisons.

E3.justification: The added semantic-segmentation experiment introduces SemanticFPN training for 40K iterations, batch size 32, initial learning rate 0.0002, and polynomial decay with power 0.9. It reports mIoU and backbone latency at 512 × 512 resolution. Existing experimental protocols are retained.

E4.justification: The token-mixer, head, fusion, state-count, and normalization ablations remain unchanged, as do the memory, receptive-field, VSSD replacement, and device-scaling analyses. New Appendix H provides explanatory discussion without additional ablation or robustness evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2 continues the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table 7 reports 41.3% mIoU and 0.45 ms backbone latency for EfficientViM-M4, versus 39.7% and 0.94 ms for EdgeViT-XXS; PVTv2-B0 and FastViT-SA12 obtain 37.2% and 38.0% mIoU. All 13 matched existing tables retain their entries and values, and retained result figures are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix G adds a mathematical qualification concerning C = xin WC: a fixed projection cannot generally enforce the diagonal-C condition for arbitrary inputs, so the stated equivalence does not establish generalization between the methods. Proposition 1, its assumptions, and its algebraic proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The core contributions remain HSM-SSD, multi-stage hidden-state fusion, and a design minimizing memory-bound operations, with the same ImageNet speed-accuracy claim. Revisions to the abstract and conclusion emphasize mechanisms already described in v1.

C2.justification: The new Appendix G remark explicitly limits the equivalence result to special conditions and inputs. Appendix H expands the fusion explanation through deep supervision and an ensemble of representations from different stages, extending v1's discussion of stronger hidden representations and low- and high-level features.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 adds the segmentation head, training budget, batch size, learning rate, scheduler, and evaluation resolution for ADE20K. Existing training recipes, architecture specifications, device information, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for ADE20K, Panoptic FPN, Deeply-Supervised Nets, U-Net++, DenseNet, and FPN. Appendix H connects multi-stage fusion to deep supervision and multi-scale representations; the main related-work positioning is largely retained.

P1.justification: V2 edits the abstract, introduction, method explanations, and conclusion. It moves distillation into Section 4.1, COCO experiments into Section 4.2, and high-resolution experiments into Appendix B, while adding Appendix H, acknowledgments, and updated affiliations. Most existing prose and the overall structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the ADE20K table, moves the COCO table into the main text, and relocates the high-resolution table and figure to the supplement. Main-text Figure 6 is removed while its ablation results remain in tables and supplementary plots. Retained figure images are identical, with limited caption and layout edits.

improvement.justification: The ADE20K experiment adds direct evidence for semantic-segmentation applicability with concrete training details. The new theoretical caveat reduces the risk of overinterpreting Proposition 1, and Appendix H clarifies the fusion rationale. These are useful, bounded gains; the central method and most empirical evidence remain unchanged.
